newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota plantings progress, emergence is slow.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota plantings progress, emergence is slow.

text.p: Dry weather in most parts of North Dakota in the week ended on Sunday allowed planting progress of spring wheat, durum and oats to move ahead of average, the state's agricultural statistics service said.
"Emergence of all crops was behind average, in part due to the cool temperatures," the agency said. "Wire worm damage was reported in early emerged small grains."
Spring wheat condition was rated 80 percent good to excellent, 19 percent fair.
Spring wheat planted 79 pct vs 49 week ago, 55 year ago, 77 on a five-year average.
Spring wheat emerged 38 pct vs 10 w/a, 24 y/a, 54 avge.
Durum wheat planted 72 pct vs 35 w/a, 44 y/a, 69 avge.
Durum wheat emerged 27 pct vs 7 w/a, 14 y/a, 40 avge.
Oats planted 83 pct vs 47 w/a, 51 y/a, 75 avge.
Oats emerged 35 pct vs 5 w/a, 19 y/a, 52 avge.
Corn planted 78 pct vs 51 w/a, 52 y/a, 68 avge.
Corn emerged 28 pct vs 6 w/a, 13 y/a, 31 avge.
Soybeans planted 45 pct vs 16 w/a, 16 y/a, 55 avge.
Soybeans emerged 3 pct vs nil w/a, nil y/a, 9 avge.
Sugarbeets planted 93 pct vs 76 w/a, 67 y/a, 89 avge.
Sugarbeets emerged 37 pct vs 18 w/a, 18 y/a, 60 avge.
Sunflowers planted 16 pct vs 2 w/a, 9 y/a, 30 avge.
Sunflowers emerged 1 pct vs nil w/a, nil y/a, 5 avge.
Canola planted 76 pct vs 30 w/a, n/a y/a, n/a avge.
Canola emerged 23 pct vs 2 w/a, n/a y/a, n/a avge.
Flaxseed planted 47 pct vs 15 w/a, 14 y/a, 44 avge.
Flaxseed emerged 11 pct vs nil w/a, 3 y/a, 16 avge.

Pasture and range was in mostly good condition and provided roughly 90 percent of roughage requirements for livestock, it said. Grain and concentrate supplies were rated 81 percent adequate, 2 percent surplus.
((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720))
